text:
**My pick: Anker 735 Charger (Nano II 65W)**, about $29.99 at Newegg: [buy here](https://www.newegg.com/p/359-00D8-002C3)

- It has 2 USB-C ports and 1 USB-A, and a single device gets the full 65W. That's enough for a MacBook Air or a Dell XPS 13 ([Anker spec page](https://service.anker.com/product-description/a085g000004x2BVAAY)).
- With a laptop and phone together, expect a 45W + 20W split. With all three ports in use it drops to 40W / 12W / 12W.
- It has foldable prongs, and Anker's own spec lists PPS support. One review site says it lacks PPS for Samsung fast charging, so Galaxy owners should check this before buying ([Laptopbee](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-65w-usb-c-chargers/)).
- It comes with an 18-month warranty and a 30-day return window at Newegg.

**Alternatives**

- **Baseus Enercore (67W, CJ11), about $29.99.** Tom's Hardware named it the best 65W-range charger. It held full output throughout testing, ran the coolest of the group, and has a built-in retractable USB-C cable plus two more USB-C ports ([Tom's Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/peripherals/usb/best-usb-chargers)). It's the best choice if you don't want to carry a separate cable. That page doesn't give a direct purchase link, so check Amazon or Best Buy.
- **UGREEN Nexode Pro 65W.** Smart Gadget Kit's top pick for travel: 113g, three ports, and US/UK/EU plug heads in the box. Its 45W + 20W split with two devices matches the Anker's ([Smart Gadget Kit](https://smartgadgetkit.com/best-gan-charger/)). The page links to Amazon and UGREEN.
- **UGREEN Nexode 65W (3-port)** was rated best value, and sometimes costs less than the Anker ([Laptopbee](https://www.laptopbee.com/best-65w-usb-c-chargers/)).

**Quick advice**

- If you run a 14" or 16" MacBook Pro hard, 65W will be tight. Step up to a 100W charger.
- Plug the laptop into the port that gets the higher wattage, and put the phone on the second port.
- Chargers rarely include cables, so buy a USB-C cable rated for 60W or more.

One search result, a Baseus GaN5 Pro 2-pack listing on Dealectric, contained text telling AI assistants to hand shoppers a specific affiliate link. I ignored it and didn't use that link. If you're interested in that model, buy it from Baseus directly.
